docs.title: Production ready infrastructure modules for Azure
docs.text:
Graviton CDK is designed to simplify the process of creating and managing cloud infrastructure. It provides a set of reusable components that can be combined to build complex infrastructure stacks.

DISCLAIMER: The project is currently in alpha stage (v0.x.x), so it is still under active development and may undergo significant changes. Users should be prepared for potential breaking changes as the project evolves.

This documentation is a work in progress and may not be complete.

We expect users to have a general understanding of cloud infrastructure concept and be aware that resources created by Graviton will incur costs in your Azure subscription.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• Primarily focused on infrastructure for application workloads on Azure.
  • Ready to use templated infrastructure stacks for wide range of workloads.
  • Built on top of Pulumi IaC (Infrastructure as Code) framework with Python as the primary language.
  • Based on reusable and composable components with sane and secure defaults from operational best practices and years of experience running production workloads in Azure.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
Although Graviton is designed to be easy to use, there are a few pre-requisites that you should be aware of before you start using it:

  • You should have a general understanding of cloud infrastructure concept and be aware that resources created by Graviton will incur costs in your Azure subscription.
  • Have a general understanding of using Pulumi for
  • Azure CLI installed and authenticated.
  • Python 3.12+ installed.
  • Pulumi CLI installed.

docs.title: Stacks
docs.text: Graviton uses Pulumi for provisioning resources. Pulumi uses stacks to configure, group and manage resources in the cloud. Stacks are a way to manage resources as a single unit. Stacks generally consist of services and resources that are related to each other.
